question: Can the pointwise formula [t-1]P-pi(P) on each frozen extension cell be reconstructed as one base-field rational x-map of predicted degrees (N,N-1), with poles exactly at nonidentity base points, enough regular samples for the proved strict separation bound, and identical coefficients across extension degrees?

field_construction.representation: GF(p)[u] modulo the lexicographically first monic irreducible polynomial of the frozen degree

pointwise_map: P maps to [t-1]P-pi(P), with pi the coordinatewise p-power Frobenius; infinity is retained as a pole value

predicted_map_model.finite_poles: x-values of nonidentity E(F_p) points, with multiplicity equal to the affine x-fiber size

reconstruction.denominator: the monic product over observed pole x-values, each repeated by its source x-fiber multiplicity
reconstruction.first_numerator: degree-at-most-N interpolation of x(image)*D(x) on the first N+1 regular x-values in canonical field-index order
reconstruction.second_numerator: the same interpolation on the last N+1 regular x-values
reconstruction.normalization: ascending coefficients; denominator monic; every recovered coefficient must lie in the embedded base field

independent_verifier.method: separate Python field/group implementation and separate Lagrange interpolation; reconstruct every pointwise image, pole and coefficient

positive_checks: the two points above every paired x-value have the same image x-coordinate or are both mapped to infinity
the pole x-count equals the independently enumerated base-field affine x-count and total pole multiplicity equals N-1
the reconstructed denominator has degree N-1 and is nonzero exactly on every frozen regular sample
both canonical interpolation windows recover identical degree-N numerators
the recovered numerator and denominator coefficients all lie in F_p
the reconstructed fraction matches every regular sample and its numerator is nonzero at every pole
coefficient encodings are identical across all frozen extension degrees of the same base curve
controls: adding one to the numerator constant coefficient rejects every regular sample
adding one to the denominator constant coefficient destroys every observed pole
restricting the regular sample to exactly 2*N-1 is recorded as failing the strict Lean cardinality premise
measurements: pole and regular distinct-x counts, pole multiplicity, predicted degrees and strict separation margin
both full numerator encodings and the denominator encoding
point-pair consistency, full-sample mismatches, pole cancellation failures and control rejection counts
producer and verifier elapsed nanoseconds as single-run diagnostics

acceptance.primary: every positive check passes in all eight cells, every exact field matches the independent replay, and all three base-curve coefficient families are stable across extension degrees
acceptance.controls: both coefficient mutations reject at every applicable sample and the equality-boundary premise fails at exactly 2*N-1 samples
acceptance.failure_policy: retain every row and do not replace a curve, degree, interpolation window, degree model, pole rule, check, or control

claim_boundary: This reconstructs finite-panel rational x-coordinate candidates for the pointwise formula and tests the predicted degree/pole model. It does not independently prove deg(V-1)=N, identify the candidate as a scheme morphism over the algebraic closure, transport it to the completed local series, solve ECDLP, or establish runtime or asymptotic improvement.
